title: Silverpine - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
topics: Dedicated GPU sizing and reserved capacity
summary: Intro discovery to size Redwood Dedicated for Silverpine's LLM inference. Key concerns: predictable latency for user-facing scoring, isolation for sensitive PII, burst handling for end-of-day batch jobs, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Action: send sizing/pricing, security docs, and propose pilot test with 8-GPU pool.
action_items: Avery Chen - Send Dedicated capacity pricing options + example contract language - due 2026-03-08
Samir Patel - Prepare recommended sizing for 100 qps 512-token median, include GPU type and expected p99 latency - due 2026-03-10
Priya Singh - Share internal compliance checklist and confirm SOC2 scope for inference data - due 2026-03-09
next_steps: Avery to send pricing and security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, network diagrams)
Schedule 60m pilot kickoff with infra + ML (tentative week of 2026-03-15)
Run small benchmark with customer's sample workload on Redwood Dedicated test pool
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Avery, AE on Redwood, and Samir with me is our SE.
[00:12] Rachel Moore: Hi, Rachel here. Head of ML at Silverpine. Tom and Priya are on as well.
[00:18] Tom Alvarez: Hey everyone. Infra lead.
[00:20] Priya Singh: Priya, security.
[00:24] Samir Patel: Great, thanks. Quick agenda — understand your workload, latency/cost constraints, security needs, and then go through Dedicated options.
[00:35] Rachel: Sounds good. To start, we run a real-time scoring service for loan origination and fraud. Latency target is pretty tight — p95 under 350ms ideally, p99 under 800ms. We currently do on-prem GPUs but want to offload some workloads.
[00:52] Tom: We also have nightly batch jobs that peak at 10k reqs over a couple hours, so burst capacity is important.
[01:02] Avery: Cool. Are you evaluating hosted Redwood or Dedicated?
[01:06] Rachel: We're mainly interested in Dedicated for isolation and data residency. Don't want customer PII ever touching multi-tenant GPUs.
[01:12] Priya: Also need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO (SAML). SOC2 is a must.
[01:20] Samir: Absolutely. Our Dedicated product supports customer VPC/private networking and KMS/HSM integrations, plus audit logging. SOC2 reports and ISO docs are in our security pack — we'll share those.
[01:34] Rachel: Great. On sizing — our current model is a 7B transformer quantized to int8 on RTX A10G equivalents, typical seq len around 512 but some requests go up to 1k. We need to estimate GPUs.
[01:50] Samir: Okay, median 512, 1k tail. For 100 qps steady with 512 tokens median, rough ballpark is X GPUs — (notes) sorry, my transcript tool scrubbed the specific number — but we can calculate. Are you seeing many long sequences simultaneously or are they spread?
[02:10] Rachel: Usually spread, but during batch windows we get bursts of longer sequences.
[02:18] Tom: Also want predictable latency; we prefer reserved capacity rather than pure autoscale to avoid noisy neighbors.
[02:24] Avery: Makes sense. Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with configurable burst capacity. You can reserve baseline capacity for steady qps and allow burst into oversubscription or burst VMs. Samir, want to explain the burst policy?
[02:36] Samir: Sure — we support a primary reserved pool and a burst pool that spins up additional nodes. For strict isolation we can keep burst within your dedicated tenancy but it costs more. There's also pre-warmed capacity to reduce cold-starts for KV cache and model warmup. Note: pre-warm helps p99 but has cost.
[02:58] Priya: How fast does the burst spin up? We need to know for end-of-day surges.
[03:04] Samir: Typical spin-up is 2-6 minutes depending on region and image. For faster response we recommend a small pre-warmed buffer — e.g., keep 1-2 GPUs hot so latency stays low.
[03:16] Rachel: So for us maybe 8 GPUs reserved and 4 pre-warmed? Tom, what do you think?
[03:21] Tom: Could work. How does scheduling affect multi-model support? We host multiple model versions for canaries.
[03:28] Samir: We support model version pinning on routes and canary routing with percentage rollouts. On Dedicated you can pin VMs to specific model images or let the orchestrator multiplex. Multiplexing increases utilization but can slightly increase tail latency under contention.
[03:44] Rachel: That tradeoff is important. For loan decisions we probably pin to avoid variability.
[03:50] Priya: Security question — network topology. We need a VPC peering option and no public internet egress for inference.
[03:57] Avery: Dedicated supports customer-managed VPC and private endpoints. We can remove outbound internet access and route logs to your S3.
[04:05] Priya: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys?
[04:08] Samir: Yes, KMS integration with customer keys is supported; HSM options for enterprise as well. We'll include the integration guide.
[04:15] Rachel: On compliance — SOC2 plus retention windows. Can we get audit logs for token-level events?
[04:20] Samir: We provide per-route request/response logs and token-level cost breakdown in the Console. For PII-sensitive data we support redaction at ingestion or not logging responses.
[04:33] Rachel: Good. Cost — we need an approximation. Our CFO will want per-token and reserved monthly.
[04:38] Avery: We'll send a pricing example: reserved pool monthly + per-token compute floor. For burst usage you can pay on top. I'll include an example showing cost vs latency for different pool sizes.
[04:50] Tom: Benchmarks — can we run our workload?
[04:54] Samir: Yes, we can run a short benchmark on a test Dedicated pool. Typically we ask for a representative sample of requests (1000-5000) and we run p95/p99 measurements. We can supply an instrumented harness.
[05:07] Rachel: How long would a pilot last? We want 2-4 weeks to validate production metrics.
[05:12] Avery: 2-4 weeks is standard. Pilot would be in your VPC with limited routing. We'll instrument metrics and compare latencies and costs.
[05:20] Priya: Legal — any standard contract restrictions we should know? Data residency, termination, and SLAs?
[05:26] Avery: We have SLA options for Dedicated. Standard enterprise T&Cs cover data residency and we can add clauses for termination and data retention.
[05:34] Rachel: Any gotchas with quantized models or custom kernels?
[05:38] Samir: Our runtime supports common quantizations (int8, q4) and we pick kernels per model. For very custom kernel work we have a performance onboarding path — it can add 1-2 weeks for kernel tuning.
[05:51] Tom: What's the typical GPU type? NVidia A10G? A100?
[05:55] Samir: We offer A10G-equivalent and A100 depending on region and commitment. The pricing differs; we'll show both.
[06:05] Rachel: Do you have examples of customers with similar needs?
[06:08] Avery: Yes, a couple of fintechs run Dedicated with strict isolation and burst needs. We'll anonymize and share case notes.
[06:15] Rachel: Great.
[06:18] [06:18] Speaker 1 (background): we had a question about caching -
[06:21] Samir: On caching — we support prefix/KV caching to reduce per-token compute. For scoring it's often effective since many contexts repeat. But cache invalidation needs app logic.
[06:32] Priya: Can cache be stored on customer-managed storage?
[06:36] Samir: Yes, cache can be in your VPC-backed Redis or in our managed cache with encryption.
[06:42] Rachel: For SLA we'd like explicit p99 numbers. What's a conservative estimate for p99 on an A10G with model size 7B, 512 tokens?
[06:50] Samir: Conservatively, p99 around 600-800ms if you pre-warm and pin model. Without pinning and cold starts it can be 1.2s+. We'll include more precise numbers after we run your sample.
[07:05] Tom: Regarding autoscaling policies — can we set rules based on queue length or latency?
[07:11] Samir: Yes, autoscale can be threshold-based (CPU/GPU utilization, queue latency). But for strict SLOs we recommend a reserved baseline plus scale rules to limit variance.
[07:22] Rachel: How do you handle graceful degradation if capacity is constrained? Fallback to smaller model?
[07:27] Samir: We support smart routing and fallback policies — route to a lower-cost/quality model, or to hosted fallback if Dedicated is overloaded. Policies are configurable per-route.
[07:38] Priya: Any change management for model rollouts? We want canaries and automatic rollback on regressions.
[07:44] Samir: Rollouts with canary percent and automatic rollback on monitoring alerts is supported. You can tie to eval sets to detect quality regressions.
[07:56] Rachel: Good. On the cost example, if we reserve 8 GPUs and burst to 4 on peak, can you ballpark monthly?
[08:04] Avery: We'll give an example in the doc; depends on GPU type and region. Expect reserved baseline + burst usage billed hourly. We'll show modeled cost for A10G vs A100.
[08:15] Tom: Network egress — we need to keep egress internal for compliance; any bandwidth caps?
[08:19] Samir: No mandatory egress to public internet; we can keep traffic in VPC and route logs to your storage. Bandwidth limits depend on instance type but are usually sufficient. We'll include network diagrams.
[08:31] [08:31] Rachel: Ok, let's talk timeline. We want pilot by mid-March and production by mid-April if pilot goes well.
[08:39] Avery: That timeline's doable. I'll follow up with a proposed pilot plan.
[08:44] Priya: We'll need security review docs before pilot.
[08:47] Avery: We'll attach SOC2, encryption, and SAML guides.
[08:51] Samir: For the benchmark, please send a sample dataset and representative request shapes (percentiles of seq length). We need that to size properly.
[08:59] Rachel: Will do.
[09:02] Avery: Quick recap — action items: we'll send pricing/security pack, Samir will produce sizing estimate, and we'll schedule pilot kickoff. Anything else?
[09:12] Tom: Can you include an example contract term for reserved capacity and termination?
[09:16] Avery: Yes.
[09:18] Priya: Please redact token-level logs in the pilot unless requested.
[09:22] Samir: Noted — default redaction unless you opt-in.
[09:26] Rachel: Thanks everyone — this was helpful.
[09:29] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and scheduling.
[54:50] [end]
